belongs_to: "The letter A has a vertical line of symmetry. So, to cut out the letter 'A'- 1. Fold a paper in half. 2. Draw half of the letter A along the fold. 3. Cut along the outline. 4. Open the paper to see the full letter A."
description: Four small pictures in a 2 x 2 layout inside a cream rounded panel (the panel is shared with the H steps below it), each with a light-green tag: Step 1 top-left, Step 2 top-right, Step 3 middle-left, Step 4 middle-right. Step 1: a flat orange (peach) square sheet with ONE dashed red vertical line through the exact middle of the square (the fold line; it runs a little above and below the sheet); the left half is a slightly darker orange than the right half. Step 2: the folded paper, an orange rectangle half as wide as the square (same height), with a dotted outline of the LEFT half of the letter A drawn on it: the slanting stroke '/' going up to the top-right corner plus the left half of the crossbar, with the straight (fold) edge on the right side of the rectangle. Step 3: the cut-out piece, orange, shaped like '/' with a short crossbar stub pointing right, dotted outline, vertical cut edge on its right. Step 4: the full letter A in orange (both legs, crossbar, triangular hole), no dotted lines. Colour is orange in all four steps; the only red marking is the dashed fold line in Step 1.
unclear: Exact width of the Step 2 rectangle (about half of the Step 1 square) is judged by eye.

belongs_to: "The letter H has two lines of symmetry. 1. Fold the paper into one-fourth (once vertically, once horizontally). 2. Draw one-fourth of the letter H along the fold. 3. Cut along the outline. 4. Open the paper to see the full letter H."
description: Four small pictures in a 2 x 2 layout under the A steps, in the same cream panel, each with a lilac tag: Step 1 middle-left, Step 2 middle-right, Step 3 bottom-left, Step 4 bottom-right. Step 1: a flat green square sheet with TWO dashed red lines crossing at its exact centre, one vertical and one horizontal (both extend a little beyond the sheet); the four quarters are slightly different greens (top-left darkest, bottom-right lightest). Step 2: a green square one-fourth the area of the Step 1 square (half the side) placed over a dotted outline of the whole letter H; the small square sits at the top-left of the H outline and contains the top-left quarter of the H, i.e. the upper half of the left stem and the left half of the crossbar (an L-shape in dotted outline); the rest of the H outline is dotted and uncovered to the right and below. Step 3: the cut-out piece, dark green, shaped like the letter L (vertical stroke with a short foot pointing right at the bottom), dotted outline. Step 4: the full letter H in green (two vertical stems joined by a crossbar). Colour is green in all four steps; the only red marking is the pair of dashed fold lines in Step 1.
unclear: Which quarter of the H the small square covers in Step 2 is read as the top-left quarter (the L-shaped piece in Step 3 supports this).

belongs_to: "Which of the following alphabet cutouts can be made by just drawing half or quarter of the letter? ... E N X T K V O" and the three blanks (horizontal line of symmetry / vertical line of symmetry / both)
description: A single row of seven plain upper-case sans-serif letters, left to right: E (pale green), N (olive/khaki), X (pink), T (teal), K (blue), V (orange), O (purple). Seven letters in total, evenly spaced, all the same size, upright, no dots, no lines, no fold lines or any marking on them. Each letter is a single flat colour. The O is a ring (round, hollow).

belongs_to: "Use lines of symmetry to make paper cutouts of diya, boat, and other designs. Look along the border of the page to find the pictures."
description: 16 small flat 'paper cutout' pictures spread around the border of the page, 4 on each side; every one is two-toned (left half and right half in slightly different shades) with a vertical centre crease, and every one is mirror-symmetric about that vertical line. Top edge, left to right: (1) upward-pointing arrow (olive/khaki, top-left corner); (2) diya (clay lamp: brown curved bowl with a yellow flame above); (3) leaf (green, pointed top, short stem down); (4) flower (pale-yellow scalloped petals around a dark-brown centre, top-right corner). Right edge, top to bottom: (5) leaf (green, egg-shaped, short stem down); (6) club-style trefoil (blue-grey, three round lobes and a stem); (7) heart (rose red); (8) open umbrella (pink, straight handle down). Bottom edge, right to left: (9) paper boat (brown: triangular sail above a wide trapezium hull); (10) four-lobed clover (yellow: lobes at top, left, right, bottom); (11) round disc (green circle); (12) paper dart/aeroplane (grey, pointed top, narrow). Left edge, bottom to top: (13) kite (blue diamond with a small yellow tail below); (14) butterfly (yellow, two pairs of wings, two feelers); (15) bow-tie (purple); (16) fir/pine tree (green, tiered). Only the diya and the boat are named by the text.
unclear: Whether shape 10 has four lobes or is a three-lobed clover with a bottom lobe hidden: read as four lobes.

section: Let Us Make a Windmill Firki
belongs_to: "Follow the steps given below to make your own firki. 1. Take a square paper. ... 9. Push the pin through a stick or straw."
description: Eight small gold/yellow paper pictures down the right-hand side, one beside each of steps 1 to 8 (step 9 has no separate picture). Step 1: a plain flat square, no creases. Step 2: a right-angled isosceles triangle with the right angle at the bottom-right (vertical right side, horizontal base), a dashed crease along the slanting side from bottom-left up to top-right. Step 3: two pictures side by side: on the left a square with ONE dashed diagonal crease from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner (upper-left half darker gold); on the right a right-angled triangle with the right angle at the bottom-left (vertical left side, horizontal base) and a dashed slanting side from top-left down to bottom-right. Step 4: a square showing BOTH diagonals as dashed creases (an X), the four small triangles in different gold shades (left lightest). Step 5: the same square with the X creases and a pair of scissors (silver blades, orange handles) at the lower-right; a white cut slit runs along the lower-right arm of the X from the corner towards the centre and stops about halfway. Step 6: the cut square with one triangle's corner folded in towards the centre, a pale curled flap visible just below-left of the centre and a notch in the bottom edge. Step 7: the windmill shape with four folded vanes meeting at the centre, no pin and no stick yet. Step 8: the same windmill with a red pin dot at the centre and a thin brown stick going straight down from the centre.
unclear: Step 6: exactly which corner is folded and the shape of the notch are small in the picture and read only approximately.

section: Let Us Make a Windmill Firki
belongs_to: "Observe the dot in the firki. Does the firki look the same after 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, and a full turn? ______"
description: A row of FIVE identical gold four-vane windmills (firkis), each with a red/salmon pin dot at the centre and a thin brown stick going straight down. Under each windmill is a lilac rounded label, left to right: 'Initial position', '1/4 turn', '1/2 turn', '3/4 turn', 'Full turn'. Each windmill has ONE small green dot on a vane, the only thing that differs between the five pictures; the vanes look identical in all five. Position of the green dot relative to the pin: Initial position - just above and slightly left of the pin; 1/4 turn - to the right of the pin (slightly above); 1/2 turn - below the pin (slightly right); 3/4 turn - to the left of the pin (slightly below); Full turn - back above and slightly left of the pin, same as the initial position. So the dot goes up -> right -> down -> left -> up, i.e. a clockwise turn. In the Initial position picture only, a red dashed arrow starts at the pin and points up and to the right (north-east), showing the starting direction. The stick stays vertical in all five pictures (only the vanes are turned).
unclear: The dot positions are described relative to the pin as seen on the page; the exact distance of the dot from the pin was not measured.

section: Let Us Make a Windmill Firki
belongs_to: "Observe the letters below. Do they look the same when turned? Dots have been marked on the letters ... Original letter / 1/4 turn / 1/2 turn / 3/4 turn / Full turn / Rotational symmetry (Yes/No)" (table with H done, I, X, Y to fill)
description: A table with a dark blue-grey rounded border: 6 columns and 5 rows (1 header row + 4 letter rows). Header row (teal-green fill): 'Original letter', '1/4 turn', '1/2 turn', '3/4 turn', 'Full turn', 'Rotational symmetry (Yes/No)'. Every letter is drawn as a thick rounded-stroke shape with a red dot with a white highlight at its centre/pivot and tiny white dots that mark the orientation. Row 1 (H, purple, the completed example row): Original = upright H with white dots at the top ends of both stems; 1/4 turn = H turned sideways (two horizontal bars joined by a short vertical piece in the middle), with a black dashed outline of the original upright H (two tall rounded stem outlines and the crossbar) drawn behind it, white dots at the right ends of the two bars; 1/2 turn = upright H again with the white dots now at the bottom ends of both stems; 3/4 turn = sideways H with the dashed outline of the upright H, white dots at the left ends of the two bars; Full turn = upright H, white dots at the top (same as Original); last column text: 'Yes, at 1/2 turn'. Row 2: first cell shows the letter I (a green vertical rounded bar, red dot at its middle, one white dot near the top); the other 5 cells are empty white. Row 3: first cell shows the letter X (blue, red dot where the strokes cross, white dots at the two upper arm tips); other 5 cells empty. Row 4: first cell shows the letter Y (khaki/tan, white dots at the two upper arm tips, red dot placed low on the stem, below the junction of the arms and not at the centre of the letter); other 5 cells empty. Total body cells to fill: 3 rows x 5 cells = 15 (4 turn cells + 1 Yes/No cell per row); only row 1 is filled.
unclear: The letter in row 2 is a plain vertical bar and is read as capital I.
Exact positions of the white orientation dots in the sideways H pictures (right ends / left ends of the bars) are read from a small picture.

belongs_to: "Find symmetry in the digits. Which digit(s) have reflection symmetry? Which digit(s) have rotational symmetry? Which digit(s) have both rotational and reflection symmetries?"
description: A single row of the ten digits in the order 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 0, each in a different flat colour with a thin blue outline, plain rounded sans-serif shapes: 1 = a plain vertical bar with no flag and no foot (light orange/yellow); 2 = blue; 3 = light green; 4 = olive/khaki (open style, with the diagonal stroke); 5 = pink/salmon; 6 = teal; 7 = blue; 8 = orange (two stacked loops); 9 = purple; 0 = blue (oval ring). Ten digits in total, all upright, same height, no dots or lines on them.

belongs_to: "Now, let us look at the following numbers: 11, 1001. Do these have (a) rotational symmetry, (b) reflection symmetry or (c) both symmetries?"
description: Two numbers printed inline in the text, separated by a comma: a 2-digit number made of two digits 1 and a 4-digit number 1 0 0 1. In this book's type the digit 1 is drawn as a plain vertical bar (no flag, no foot), the same bar as the '1' in the digit row, and the 0 is an oval ring: so they look like '||' and '|00|'. Plain black text, no colour, no boxes.
unclear: The printed text extraction reads '|| , |00|'; read here as the numbers 11 and 1001 with the digit 1 drawn as a bar.

belongs_to: "(a) Does the design have rotational symmetry? Yes/No. (b) Try to change the design by adding some shape(s) so that the new design looks the same after a 1/2 turn. ... (c) ... after 1/4 turn. (d) Do the new designs have reflection symmetry?"
description: A design of flat light-blue shapes (one single colour, no outlines) on white, made of 5 pieces: one central circle (diameter d); one triangle on each side of it. Left of the circle: an isosceles triangle whose vertical base touches the circle's left edge and whose apex points LEFT (away from the circle). Right of the circle: an identical triangle whose vertical base touches the circle's right edge and whose apex points RIGHT (away from the circle). Above the circle: an isosceles triangle whose horizontal base is at the top and whose apex points DOWN and touches the top of the circle. Below the circle: an identical triangle whose horizontal base is at the bottom and whose apex points UP and touches the bottom of the circle. Each triangle's base and height are both about 1.3 times the circle's diameter. Plus ONE more separate circle of the same size as the central circle, placed at the far right on the same horizontal line, just touching the apex of the right-pointing triangle. Total: 2 circles and 4 triangles; the extra circle on the right only is what stops the design from being the same after a half turn.

belongs_to: "Does this design look the same after 1/2 turn? ______ Does the design look the same after 1/4 turn? ______"

belongs_to: "Colour the square given in the adjoining figure using two colours so that the design looks the same after every 1/4 turn. How many times does this shape look the same during a full turn?"

These lines cut the square into 8 equal triangular parts (each meeting at the centre). All parts are uncoloured (blank) for the student to colour. No labels.
unclear: 'How many times does this shape look the same during a full turn?' stands directly after the colouring instruction; it is read as referring to the coloured design in this square, but it could also refer to the 2 x 2 square above.

belongs_to: "Does this shape have reflection symmetry? If yes, draw its line(s) of symmetry. Does it have rotational symmetry? If yes, at which turn? Does it have both symmetries?"
description: A composite shape of flat pieces with a thin white gap and soft shadow between them: 4 blue squares of equal size in a 2 x 2 block (2 squares in the top row, 2 in the bottom row), and 4 tan/khaki triangles, 2 on the left and 2 on the right. On the left of each row of squares is an isosceles triangle whose vertical base lies along the left edge of the left square and whose apex points LEFT; on the right of each row is an identical triangle whose vertical base lies along the right edge of the right square and whose apex points RIGHT. Each triangle's base equals one square side and its height is also about one square side. The overall shape is 2 squares + 2 triangles wide and 2 squares tall; no lines are drawn on it.

belongs_to: "Wooden Block Print ... Artisans use carved wooden blocks to print designs on fabric." (the 'Wooden Block' and 'Print' pictures beside the text)
description: Two tall rounded cream tiles side by side, each with an orange rounded tag on top: 'Wooden Block' (left) and 'Print' (right). Wooden Block: a photograph of a dark-brown rectangular carved block, portrait orientation (height about twice the width), with a carved light design: two diamonds (squares turned 45 degrees) stacked one above the other, each diamond drawn with a double outline and holding a circular motif (concentric rings with a ring of small dots and four small petal shapes up, down, left, right); around the diamonds are about 14 leaf shapes arranged in pairs along the two long sides and at the four corners. Print: the same design printed in black ink on cream cloth, with the design lines dark on the light background (the block's light design appears dark): two stacked diamonds with the same circular motifs and the same leaf shapes. The print is the same pattern as the block, not a different one.
unclear: Exact number of leaf shapes (about 14) is estimated from a small photograph.

belongs_to: "Below are images of wooden blocks and a part of their prints. Match each block to its correct print by drawing a line. One is done for you."
description: Two rows of five rounded cream photograph tiles. Top row (blocks), left to right, each labelled in the bottom-right corner of its tile: (i) a paisley (mango-shape) block, grey-brown, scalloped outer edge, a leaf/fern drawn inside; (ii) a lotus-flower block with pointed petals, a teardrop in the middle and leaves at the base; (iii) a round rosette block with a scalloped edge and a flower with 8 petals; (iv) a half-round fan block (semicircle with a scalloped curved edge, radiating fan lines and a small circle at the bottom centre); (v) a tall dark-brown rectangular block carved with a flower on a stem with leaves. Bottom row (prints), left to right, labelled at the bottom-left corner of each tile: (a) a blue half-flower print with the straight edge on the left (the right half of a rosette); (b) a green half print of a stem with leaves and a bud with the straight edge on the right (left half); (c) a teal half print with scalloped curved edge, straight edge on the left (right half of a paisley); (d) a yellow half lotus print with a leaf, straight edge on the right (left half); (e) a red-brown half fan print with scalloped curved edge, straight edge on the right. Each print shows only HALF of its block's design, cut along a vertical line. One matching line is already drawn: a thin black straight line from the lower-right corner of block (iv) down to the top of print tile (e). No other lines.
unclear: Which side of each print (left or right half) is shown was read from small tiles; the straight edge side was judged by eye.

belongs_to: "Observe the pattern made by the wooden block below. We get the final print by using the block 4 times. ... The design A looks the same after every 1/4 turn."

Right: a large rounded tan tile with a grey tag 'Print' and the letter A at its bottom-left, showing the print in dark purple-navy ink: four copies of the leaf motif arranged as a cross, one pointing up, one down, one left, one right from the centre, each motif a feather shape with curved ribs, the thick part nearer the middle of each arm. A thin straight line runs the full width horizontally and another the full height vertically through the centre point, ending in small ticks (the stems of the four leaves). To the right of the print, a light-teal dashed box with the printed sentence 'The design A looks the same after every 1/4 turn.' (the filled-in example). Four leaf motifs in total.
unclear: The exact count of ribs on each leaf was not counted (not needed for the question).

belongs_to: "The design B looks the same after every ______ turn. This design has ______ symmetry."

Two black dashed lines run across the whole tile through the centre, one vertical and one horizontal, each passing through the middle of two opposite hearts (these are drawn lines of symmetry). Four lobes in total; the design is made by one block used 4 times at quarter turns.

Left edge, bottom to top: (15) pink long narrow scalene triangle, tilted, its sharp tip pointing down-right; (16) mauve (dusty purple-brown) bow-tie of two equal triangles touching at one vertex, the upper one reaching to the left and the lower one reaching to the right (so it looks the same after a half turn about the touching point); (17) light-green circle; (18) light-blue square (sides horizontal and vertical); (19) lilac isosceles triangle with apex up. No marks, tick or * are drawn yet.
unclear: Shape 9 (lilac ring of small tips) is very thin and small; the number of tips (about 10) and whether it is a star outline are read only roughly.
